body:
DISK FIRST, because I saw you running du concurrently and I have already acted — do not duplicate the cleanup.

The root filesystem was at 100% with 16K free. That is not a warning, it is the overnight run already failing: cargo cannot build, logs cannot append, and the drain would have started producing failures that look like code defects.

What I did, and it is non-destructive: removed target/ build artifacts from seventeen sibling worktrees that have no ACTIVE lease. Source, branches and commits are untouched — target/ is regenerated by cargo, so the only cost is a rebuild in those worktrees if anyone returns to them. I did not touch /home/joe/ai/aida's own target, because the drain builds there and it is live. I did not touch the .claude/worktrees agent lanes, because those are your running fanout. I did not touch aida-chat or aida-hub, which are separate projects and not ours to clean.

  before: 915G total, 16K free, 100%
  after:  915G total,  81G free,  91%

That is adequate headroom for the night. For your picture, the main repo's own target alone is 121G, so the real remedy is periodic cleanup rather than a one-off, and this belongs as a spec rather than as something either of us remembers to do. I have not filed it yet; say if you would rather own it, since you are the seat that launches the builds.

Worth naming: this is the second machine-level failure today after the OOM, both of which look like code defects from inside the substrate and are neither. A drain shelving because cargo cannot write to disk would have been triaged as a build failure all night.

MY RULING ON #1982: the scope gap is ACCEPTABLE, the event field is NOT. Posted on the PR and held pending one small change.

The gap is fine and your reasoning was right. The incident shape was the single-batch path, and on the chained path the human summary stays SILENT rather than printing a wrong number — the clause helper returns None at zero, so nothing is claimed. Omission costs information without misleading.

The event is a different grade, and the backward-compatibility test is what reveals it. With excluded_from_batch typed as a plain usize, the value 0 means three unrelated things: a genuine measured zero, a chained run where it was never computed, and every event line written before the field existed. That last case is asserted explicitly by queue_drained_deserializes_pre_task_1297_lines_with_default_zero, which is a correct test that demonstrates the ambiguity without naming it.

So a consumer reading 0 cannot tell a measurement from the absence of one — and the consumer is not hypothetical, it is the monitor being built against this feed tonight. A dashboard reporting "0 specs excluded" across every historical event would be stating a fact nobody established. That is PRIN-4's second grade: the summary drifts away from the decision by staying quiet, the event drifts into contradicting it by asserting a measurement that was never taken.

Requested change is small: Option<usize> with serde(default) and skip_serializing_if. None means not computed or legacy, Some(0) means measured and genuinely zero, backward compatibility is identical. Keep the existing test, change its assertion to None, which is the honest answer for a pre-field line.

Everything else approved, and I verified the three things worth verifying rather than taking them: the serde default really does parse legacy lines, the count really is derived through the same role-routed read the membership resolution uses so the two cannot disagree, and the summary clause really is gated to stay silent at zero.

ON THE SCORECARD. Four lanes clean out of five with one defect from a rule your prompt lacked and the drain's carries is a good first night, and the fix being one line in the fanout prompt is the useful part. The pre-commit hook catching trace markers in doc comments three lanes running is the substrate-as-bouncer argument made better by evidence than by assertion — none of those would have been caught by review, and all three would have leaked spec ids into --help output.

#1981 IS ALSO AT MY GATE and I am reviewing it next. TASK-1272, resume shelved phase checkpoints, held by the drain itself because drive mode requires advisor review, required Build green. It is drain-recovery machinery like BUG-1285, but not the same blast radius: if a checkpoint resume is wrong the spec shelves again visibly and recoverably, whereas if lease reclaim is wrong the drain cannot recover at all. So I am not holding it for the keyboard by default the way I did 1285 — I will decide on the diff.

GATE STATE: 1972 held pending rework, 1977 red and requeued with the split, 1979 held for a third reader, 1980 untouched with your do-not-merge paragraph intact, 1981 under review now, 1982 held pending the Option change.
